performance.driver: Sales and Marketing Expenses Sales and marketing expenses increased $6.5 million, or 35%, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the same period of fiscal year 2025. The increase was primarily due to an increase in personnel and related expenses directly associated with an increase in headcount.
Net sales increased due to 4 percent organic sales growth.

Total revenues decreased $121.1 million, or 52%, to $110.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026. The decrease was due to lower MCM Products revenue of $83.1 million, Commercial Products revenue of $31.4 million, Contracts and grants revenue of $5.5 million, and Services revenue of $1.1 million.

Operating income Our operating income increased by $51.8 million, or 55.0%, to $146.0 million, or 9.9% of revenues, for the three months ended September 25, 2026, compared with $94.2 million, or 9.6% of revenues, for the three months ended September 26, 2025. The increase was primarily due to an increase in revenues.

Net Sales Consolidated net sales for the three months ended September 30, 2026 decreased 2.4% to $481.5 million versus $493.5 million last year, reflecting higher net sales for the Retail segment, which were more than offset by lower net sales for the Foodservice segment.

Operating income was further impacted by an increase in depreciation. •E&E’s operating income was $46.7 million, an increase of 24%, and Adjusted EBITDA was $159.7 million, an increase of 12%, primarily due to the decreases in in-app purchase fees, cost of acquisition, and employee compensation expense.

Net sales for the three months ended September 30, 2026 were $337.2 million, an increase of $31.3 million, or 10.2% compared with the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in net sales was driven by favorable surcharges, improved price/mix, and higher shipment volume.

Net Sales Consolidated net sales for the three months ended September 30, 2026 decreased 2.4% to $481.5 million versus $493.5 million last year, reflecting higher net sales for the Retail segment, which were more than offset by lower net sales for the Foodservice segment.

Operating income increased $12.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared with the same period last year, due primarily to the following: •an increase of $13.5 million in revenue from new rates; and •an increase of $3.3 million in residential sales due primarily to net customer growth in Oklahoma and Texas.

Sales and Marketing Sales and marketing expenses increased by $5.8 million, or 28%, to $26.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 from $20.8 million for the comparable period in the prior year. The increase was primarily attributable to the inclusion of Stereolabs and the increase in the amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets, and costs associated with the launch of the Rev8 OS family of digital lidar sensors, offset in part by lower stock compensation and commission expenses.

Operating Income The above factors resulted in an increase of $5.7 million and $62.5 million in operating income for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, as compared to the 2025 periods. The decrease in occupancy is partially attributable to the ongoing rooms renovation at the property.
Sales prices increased 6% and 9%, respectively, reflecting a greater concentration of value-added products in the sales mix and stronger commodity markets.

Revenue Revenue increased by $61.8 million, or 16.0%, to $447.7 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to $385.8 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was primarily due to a 21.2% increase in average realized gold price, or $57.2 million, a 39.3% increase in realized silver price, or $30.8 million, and a 3.6% increase in gold ounces sold, or $9.3 million, partially offset by a 29.6% decrease in silver ounces sold, or $33.0 million.

Revenue, net Revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026, was $37.8 million, compared to revenue of $26.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $11.7 million. The increase was primarily attributable to an increase in product sales of MIPLYFFA of $11.6 million.
